Due to the late start of the project, the planned results were shifted to Y 2022. In 2021, the project managed to initiate the recruitment process of the project team, and organizing preparation for the Inception workshop,development of the Inception report and Annual project review report as per GCF requirement.

Output 2: A functional Multi-Hazard Early Warning System is established based on innovative impact modelling, risk analyses, effective regional communication and community awareness

3.1: Consultation workshop and baseline analysis for NCFS conducted. 3.2: N/A. 3.3: Technical specification for the communication boards/materials developed. Community survey designed.

Key results of the project.
Following the decision of the Inception Workshop meeting held in January 11 2022, Uzhydromet allocated an office space for the project in its premises. The key personnel (PM, TM on Climate Risks Issues and AFA) of the project assumed their duties in March 2022, while the rest of team has been formed by June 2022. Therefore, the Annual Work Plan (AWP) and budget for 2022 were revisited and adjusted taking into account the delays with recruitment of the core project staff. In addition, as per recommendation of NPC of MES during the Inception Meeting, the project in consultation with MES and Uzhydromet revisited the proposed project pilot areas and prepared an updated list of 15 districts with 44 target communities for project intervention, which was agreed and endorsed during the first virtual meeting of the Project Board held on 10 October 2022.
Furthermore, the project as per decision of the Inception Workshop meeting has procured a project vehicle, four-wheel drive Toyota Rav-4, to ensure safe travels to project sites and communities located in hazard prone areas. The procurement of the project vehicle has been discussed and agreed with RTA, IRH and CO senior management.
On 3 August 2022, the project conducted an initial informational seminar in Tashkent to present project’s goal and objectives, as well as intended results to representatives of MES, Uzhydromet, ministries and agencies. The similar events were held separately in each 7 regions, during 9-17 August 2022, where representatives of regional hokimiyats, local organizations, NGO, communities and mass media took part in these events.
More than 540 people (134 women) improved their knowledge on climate change, early warning systems, MITRA and UniMas meteorological complexes, gender equality and climate services.
On 13 October 2022, in cooperation with MES and local community leaders of Kamchik Pass, an International Day for Disaster Risk Reduction (IDDRR) was celebrated with local community children at School No. 44, located in the most disaster-prone area of Pop district in Namangan region.
Due to the late start of actual implementation of the project, the project had to adjust and make corrections to the work and implementation of activities than it was planned originally. Most major activities planned for 2022 were successfully implemented by the project, although there were minor delays and some of them switched to 2023, due to long term procurement processes or activities required close engagement and consultations with national partners and stakeholders. Furthermore, the project held its first virtual PB meeting on 10 October 2022 and regular Project Board meeting on 13 December 2022, where representatives of UNDP, MES, Uzhydromet, ministries, agencies and NGOs took part and discussed the results achieved by the project within its initial year of implementation and planned activities for 2023.
Achieved results under Output 1.
1.1. 6 new AWS purchased, installed and operational. • The project, in consultation with specialists of Uzhydromet, developed technical specifications for automated meteorological stations and 25 automatic hydrometeorological stations (MicroStep-MIS) were procured and delivered to Tashkent for further installation in pre-selected places in 2023 together with specialists of Uzhydromet. • The project conducted an assessment to identify the current conditions of 90 water gauge stations of Uzhydromet. Based on results of the assessment, the recommendations and technical specifications of the hydrological equipment required for modernization of hydrological observation network have been developed.
1.2. N/A. • With assistance of 2 international experts engaged by the project the current condition of the existing Uzhydromet’s atmospheric radar sounding network has been assessed and recommendations developed on restoring/reviving the functionality of existing C-band radars. • The assessment of the current situations in snow avalanche prone areas has been conducted and draft TOR for snow avalanche mapping model has been developed by the international expert on avalanches engaged by the project. • The assessment of the current situations in mudflow and flashflood prone areas has been conducted and draft TOR for mudflow/flashflood mapping model has been developed by the international expert on mudflows and flashfloods.
1.3 Baseline institutional capacity assessment of Uzhydromet completed. • The project is recruiting a national expert to assess the needs of Uzhydromet and develop recommendations for building capacity of experts of Uzhydromet on national and regional levels. • 16 experts (9 men and 7 women) of Uzhydromet increased their knowledge and skills on UNIMAS and MITRA communications systems during 5 days thematic trainings conducted by 2 international experts on UNIMAS and MITRA. • The project is recruiting an international expert on metrology to improve knowledge and skills of Uzhydromet experts on calibration laboratories of hydrometeorological sensors and their functionality.
Achieved results under Output 2.
2.1. N/A • The terms of reference for development of the national standard of the Republic of Uzbekistan on the system of warning and informing the population about threats or emergencies have been prepared in consultation with experts of MES. The open tender for development of the national standard will be announced in 2023.
2.2 N/A. • This activity is scheduled to be implemented in 2023.
2.3 Developed detailed technical specifications for the RCMCs data visualization system. • A draft of technical specifications for the RCMCs data visualization system (video walls, telecommunication systems, servers and ICT storage) have been developed in consultation with experts of MES. The open tender for procurement of this equipment will be announced in January 2023. • Area-specific mobile and SMS application has been developed by the IT company to deliver early warnings and information on mudflows, avalanches, landslides, and flooding risks to end-users living in disaster prone areas, including a new website of the Ministry of Emergency Situations, which is going to be finalized after its population with required information by MES.
Achieved results under Output 3.
3.1 Consultation workshop and baseline analysis for NCFS conducted. • A preliminary baseline analysis was carried out and priority areas for the preparation of the National Framework for Climate Services were identified. The project conducted a Roundtable meeting on 24 November 2022 together with a team of international and national experts, representatives of Uzhydromet, MES, respective ministries and organizations to discuss the demand and needs for NFCS, designing process and related actions, and next steps for launching development process.
3.2 N/A. • This activity is scheduled to be implemented in 2023.
3.3 Technical specification for the communication boards developed. Community survey designed. • A draft of technical specifications for outdoor information boards have been developed in consultation with experts of MES. The open tender for procurement of this equipment will be announced in January 2023. • Vulnerability assessment of communities to the risk of climate change has been conducted in 8 target communities located in 2 districts of Fergana and Namangan regions. The same assessment will also be conducted in the remaining 36 target communities of 5 regions in 2023. • The Gender Action Plan of the project has been reviewed and recommendations provided by an international gender specialist on mainstreaming and inclusion of gender aspects to project activities. • 42 people (13 men and 29 women) from national partners and project personnel increased their knowledge on gender mainstreaming and gender equality in the context of climate change. • 4 infographics on mudflows, floods, avalanches and landslides have been developed and distributed among target audience during seminars and events organized by the project in 7 pilot regions. • 4 social videos about 4 types of climate risks (mudflows, floods, avalanches and landslides) have been produced in Uzbek, Russian and English with sign language translation for broadcasting via national TV and information boards located in disaster prone areas of the country.
